title: AI handles incidents, engineers lose touch with their systems
content: AI-assisted incident response reduces routine manual work, risking a loss of human troubleshooting skills needed for complex failures. This phenomenon, known as the Ironies of Automation, parallels aviation, where pilots use simulators to maintain proficiency. To prevent engineers from losing touch with their systems, organizations should prioritize hands-on training, such as realistic incident simulations and chaos engineering. These practices are essential for maintaining the intuition and coordination skills required to resolve ambiguous, high-severity issues that automation cannot address.
